sources: CRA — Income Tax Folio S3-F10-C1 Qualified Investments (canada.ca, effective 2024-05-28) · current · ¶1.86: a TFSA is generally taxable under Part I on income from carrying on a business; ¶1.94.1: the TFSA holder is jointly and severally (solidarily) liable with the TFSA trust for the tax; whether a business is carried on is a question of fact (court factors, IT-479R)

CRA — Tax payable on non-qualified investments / TFSA issuers 'Taxes' page (canada.ca) · current · a TFSA trust that carries on a business is taxable on any income and any capital gains derived from the business; reported on a T3 return
CRA — What is a TFSA (canada.ca) · current · holders who trade with the frequency and experience of a professional trader may have the income taxed as business income
CRA IT-479R Transactions in securities (archived 1984, referenced by the Folio) · historical · factors include frequency of transactions, period of ownership, knowledge of securities markets

Example (not a CRA rule): b17/calc.py → data.json. 300 trades, mostly held 1–2 days, gains $20,000 → if a business: $20,000 taxable income in the TFSA trust; buy-and-hold growth of qualified investments: usually $0. The tax RATE on a TFSA trust was not found in the CRA pages checked, so no dollar tax is shown. Whether trading is a business depends on the facts.

titles: Day Trading in a TFSA? CRA Can Tax It
Your TFSA Isn't Always Tax-Free (Day Trading)
TFSA Day Trading: When CRA Calls It a Business
yt.description:
$20,000 in TFSA gains. Tax-free? Not if you trade like a pro.

CRA: a TFSA that carries on a business is taxable on that business income, including capital gains from the trading. Whether it's a business is a question of fact: how often you trade, how long you hold, what you know. CRA warns that trading with the frequency and experience of a professional can be taxed as business income.

Example: 300 trades in a year, most held a day or two, gains $20,000.
• If it's a business: the TFSA trust reports $20,000 of taxable income on a T3, and you're jointly liable for the tax.
• Buy and hold for the same $20,000: usually $0 tax.

How many TFSA trades did you make this year: under 10 or more? Tell me below.

Sources: CRA Income Tax Folio S3-F10-C1; CRA 'What is a TFSA'; CRA TFSA issuers 'Taxes'. Example only; general information, not tax advice.
